title: Heat Transfer

standard_text: Heat is transferred by conduction, convection and radiation; conductors and insulators; controlling heat transfer in daily life. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 1, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): conduction, convection and radiation, ways heat moves, conductors and insulators, saving heat and energy and controlling heat transfer. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Heat moves by conduction, convection and radiation.
body_html:
How to think about it

Conduction moves heat through solids (a metal spoon in hot soup). Convection moves heat in liquids and gases as warm fluid rises and cool fluid sinks, as in a pot of boiling water or a sea breeze. Radiation carries heat through empty space, such as from the Sun.

Insulators such as wood, plastic, cloth, foam and still air slow down heat transfer; conductors such as metals let heat flow easily. Light-coloured roofs and walls reflect sunlight and keep houses cooler; ceiling fans and open windows let convection carry hot air away.

Example

Why does a metal spoon in hot soup become hot?

Through the solid

Answer: conduction

Example

Why are air conditioners placed high on a wall?

Cool air sinks.

Answer: convection currents spread the cool air

Common mistakes

  • Thinking cold moves into things.
  • Thinking a blanket makes heat.
  • Thinking dark clothes keep you cooler in the sun.

faq.a: They are insulators, so the handle stays cool to hold.
Light colours reflect more sunlight, so less heat is absorbed.

items.q: How does a thermometer work?
c: The liquid inside expands when heated and rises up the tube.
items.e: Liquids expand when heated.

items.q: What happens to the particles of a substance when it is heated?
c: They move faster and spread out.
items.e: This is why most things expand when heated.

items.q: What temperature does water freeze at?
items.e: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.

items.q: The handle of a metal spoon in hot soup becomes hot. Which process mainly transfers the heat?
items.e: Heat passes through a solid or between objects in contact.

items.q: Energy from the Sun reaches the Earth across empty space. Which type of heat transfer is this mainly?
items.e: Conduction: through solids by particles vibrating. Convection: in liquids and gases as warm fluid rises. Radiation: infrared waves, even through a vacuum.

items.q: Femi observes a sea breeze blowing toward land on a sunny day. Which kind of heat transfer is this mainly?
items.e: Energy is carried by a moving liquid or gas.

items.q: The freezer compartment is at the top of an old refrigerator. Which process mainly transfers the heat?
items.e: Warmer fluid is less dense and rises; cooler fluid sinks.

items.q: What is radiation (of heat)?
